SOURCE READ 2026-08-04 under the GAP-022 rule, updated 2026-08-05. Unlike ubl, xliff's CORE is genuine work: segmentation.py (217 LOC) implements split_segment, join_segments, SegmentMapping, spanning-code closure checks and fresh-id enforcement; inline.py, text_editing.py and the reader/writer are real. Those `partial` entries are defensible pending audit.
2026-08-05 correction: the prior note here named the eight XLIFF 2.1 modules as "...Resource Data, Change Tracking, Size and Length Restriction, Validation" -- Change Tracking is not one of the eight the contract's own normative_rules name; the eighth is ITS (http://www.w3.org/2005/11/its). That error is fixed here rather than carried forward.
modules.py now gives XLIFF-MODULE-001 a programmatic coverage manifest covering all eight (Translation Candidates, Glossary, Format Style, Metadata, Resource Data, Size and Length Restriction, Validation, ITS), each PRESERVATION_ONLY with round-trip fixtures proving lossless preservation (see notes above). No typed per-module accessor exists yet, so no XLIFF-MODULE-001 obligation may be recorded above `partial`; this deepens the evidence behind `partial`, exactly like the UBL slices that moved zero obligations while making the evidence real rather than fictional. validation/validator.py still performs no schema validation, so the schema-validation clauses inside XLIFF-VALIDATE-001's `partial` entries remain overstated and still need per-obligation correction -- unchanged by this slice.
XLIFF-NOTE-001, same session: no source change. Direct experiment first (before writing any test) showed reader.py's _parse_inline is generic over every inline tag, so mrk/sm/em already survive with their exact attributes and document-order position -- which is what an overlapping span requires, since it cannot be a nested element pair. The gap was proof, not implementation; XLIFF-NOTE-001 could not be recorded `partial` before because it had zero shipped-namespace selectors, not because the behavior was absent.
XLIFF-QA-001, same session: qa.py is new source (unlike NOTE-001). Five of six named QA categories implemented with dedicated tests each; length violations explicitly left undone pending Size/Length module modeling, documented rather than stubbed. No QA-001 obligation may be recorded above `partial` -- a check existing is not the same as it being verified against every fixture the required_tests line names, and length is a real, acknowledged gap in the category set itself.
XLIFF-MERGE-001, same session: real new source (merge.py), unlike NOTE-001. SHOULD-level, and it stays SHOULD-level satisfied at `partial`: the reference adapter proves the protocol works end to end (extraction, reversible skeleton, translated merge, drift detection and refusal) but is deliberately not a real-world format adapter -- the obligation's "never claim generic extraction" clause is precisely why no such claim is made here.
Suite-level and NON-PROMOTING. The xliff suite is 265 passed with no failures (193 baseline + 22 + 11 + 25 + 14 new), but that number is still dominated by the ten shadow-package files; the shipped-namespace files now contribute 87 tests (15 + 22 + 11 + 25 + 14). A green suite here says very little about the package that would be released. Binds no individual selector outcome to an obligation, so nothing here is verification; every obligation is recorded `partial` at most.

implemented_behavior: XliffDocument.detected_version is set once, only by the reader's _parse(), from the source file's actual version attribute; `version` is the mutable, currently-declared value dumps()/dump() will write -- a plain field assignment (this model is not frozen) never touches detected_version, since there is no reconstruction step to accidentally reset it through, unlike a tree-based model would need. A freshly hand-built XliffDocument has detected_version=None. dumps() refuses (XliffWriteError) rather than silently rewriting an unsupported declared version to a supported one -- no coercion path exists.
